name: hermes
_comment: VERIFIED end-to-end 2026-07-08 against Hermes Agent v0.18.1 (macOS, local Ollama qwen3:14b @ 64k ctx) via scripts/verify_harness.py. Command shape corrected + flags re-checked 2026-08-28 against current docs (v0.20.6 era); not re-run end-to-end since. The briefing is still INLINED into the prompt rather than passed as a file path: small local models sometimes emit their file-read tool call as text instead of executing it. But the path now rides as a positional arg ($1, after --) and its content is spliced in by bash AFTER parsing — so a briefing path containing spaces works, and briefing CONTENT is never shell-evaluated (command-substitution output is inert; verified empirically). The old shape ($(head -c 2000 {briefing_file}) unquoted inline) broke silently on space-bearing paths: hermes got an EMPTY briefing while the journal recorded ok:true. cat replaces head -c 2000 because the engine already caps briefings at 4000 chars codepoint-safely — a byte-level 2000 cut could split a UTF-8 character and drop whole briefing sections. Context requirement: hermes needs >=64k context for agentic work; current docs set this on the OLLAMA side (custom Modelfile with PARAMETER num_ctx 65536, model.default pointed at it) — the model.ollama_num_ctx config key this comment used to cite does not appear in current config docs. Since v0.19.0 one-shot runs DENY dangerous commands by default (approvals single_query_mode/cron_mode) — set those, or pass --yolo, as a deliberate choice if your briefings ask for real actions. Verified on macOS only; on Windows, bash may resolve to WSL where this Windows path shape will not. Set wake_modules/wake_min_salience before running unattended (see examples/harness-configs/README.md). Ships enabled:false by default.
command: b="$(cat "$1")"; hermes -z "You were woken by ZugaMind, a cognition sidecar. Here is the briefing: $b. Act on what it asks."
